mcqs.question: Which of the following objects would NOT be considered a good reflecting surface for visible light?
mcqs.explanation: A black matte board absorbs most of the incident light and reflects very little, so it is not a good reflecting surface. Polished metal, white paper, and calm water all reflect a noticeable amount of light. Hence option C is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: A ray of light strikes a smooth, flat (plane) surface at an angle of 30° to the normal. Which statement correctly describes the reflected ray?

options.A: It will be reflected at 30° on the opposite side of the normal
options.B: It will be reflected at 60° to the normal
options.C: It will be reflected back along the same path
options.D: It will be refracted into the surface

mcqs.answer: It will be reflected at 30° on the opposite side of the normal
mcqs.explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured with respect to the normal. Therefore a 30° incident angle produces a reflected ray at 30° on the opposite side of the normal. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect behaviours.

mcqs.question: Which pair of statements correctly distinguishes regular reflection from irregular reflection?

options.A: Regular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces and produces a clear image; irregular reflection occurs on rough surfaces and scatters light in many directions.
options.B: Regular reflection occurs on rough surfaces and produces a clear image; irregular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces and scatters light.
options.C: Both regular and irregular reflection produce clear images, but only regular occurs on metal.
options.D: Irregular reflection follows the law of reflection, regular does not.

mcqs.answer: Regular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces and produces a clear image; irregular reflection occurs on rough surfaces and scatters light in many directions.
mcqs.explanation: Regular (specular) reflection happens on smooth, polished surfaces, giving a well‑defined reflected ray and a clear image. Irregular (diffuse) reflection occurs on rough surfaces, causing the incident rays to scatter in many directions, so no clear image is formed. The other options invert or misstate these facts.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate reflection to mirrors and everyday applications
mcqs.question: In which of the following everyday applications is regular (specular) reflection primarily utilized?

options.A: The use of a white wall to brighten a room
options.C: The scattering of sunlight by clouds
options.D: The diffusion of light by frosted glass

mcqs.explanation: A rear‑view mirror is a smooth, polished surface that reflects light specularly, allowing a clear, virtual image of vehicles behind the car. A white wall, clouds, and frosted glass involve diffuse (irregular) reflection or scattering, not regular reflection.

mcqs.question: What is the basic principle that describes how light behaves when it strikes a surface and bounces back?
mcqs.explanation: Reflection is the phenomenon where light rays strike a surface and are returned into the medium from which they originated. Refraction bends light as it passes into a new medium, diffraction spreads light around obstacles, and absorption converts light energy into other forms.

mcqs.question: Which of the following items can act as a reflecting surface for visible light?
mcqs.explanation: A smooth glass window reflects a portion of incident visible light, especially when the glass is clean and flat. Black cloth, charcoal, and rough stone absorb most light and scatter it irregularly, making them poor reflectors.

mcqs.question: How does a plane (flat) reflecting surface differ from a curved reflecting surface in terms of the image formed?

options.A: A plane surface forms a real, inverted image; a curved surface forms a virtual, upright image.
options.B: A plane surface forms a virtual, upright image identical in size to the object; a curved surface can form either real or virtual images that may be magnified or reduced.
options.C: Both plane and curved surfaces always produce magnified images.
options.D: Plane surfaces scatter light while curved surfaces focus light.

mcqs.answer: A plane surface forms a virtual, upright image identical in size to the object; a curved surface can form either real or virtual images that may be magnified or reduced.
mcqs.explanation: A plane mirror produces a virtual image that appears behind the mirror, upright and the same size as the object. Curved mirrors (concave or convex) can produce real or virtual images depending on object distance, and these images can be larger or smaller than the object. Options A, C, and D describe incorrect characteristics.

mcqs.question: If you look at a polished metal spoon, you notice that the image of your face is clear in some parts and fuzzy in others. Which part of the spoon is responsible for the clear image?

options.A: The curved part of the spoon
options.B: The flat (plane) part of the spoon
options.D: The back side of the spoon

mcqs.answer: The flat (plane) part of the spoon
mcqs.explanation: The flat (plane) portion of the spoon provides a smooth surface that produces regular (specular) reflection, giving a clear, virtual image. The curved part causes irregular or distorted reflection, making the image appear fuzzy. Hence option B is correct.
